Green Bay at a glance

Selling in Green Bay?

How can I sell a house fast in Green Bay?

You can list the house, sell it on your own, or take a cash offer, and the cash route is the quickest because the buyer does not wait on a lender. Which option fits depends on the condition of the house, who lives in it, and how much time you have before a payment or a move comes due.

  • Listing: the usual route for a house that shows well. It brings the widest pool of buyers and the longest timeline.
  • Selling by owner: you keep control of price and showings and do the contract and disclosure work yourself.
  • Cash offer: built for inherited houses, rentals with tenants, houses with code or repair problems, and sellers facing a deadline.

Green Bay is a city of about 106,675 people, so houses range from older homes near the river to newer blocks farther out. A buyer who pays cash will price the house on its condition and location, so gather repair estimates and permit records before you talk numbers.

What should a seller know about Green Bay itself?

Green Bay is the county seat of Brown County and sits at the mouth of the Fox River on the bay of Lake Michigan, about 90 miles north of Milwaukee. Wikipedia notes that Interstate 43 meets Interstate 41 here. The city covers 55.76 square miles, of which 45.48 are land, and about 14 percent of it lies inside the Oneida Nation reservation.

Jean Nicolet is believed to have landed near the site in 1634, and a French fur-trading post followed. Charles Michel de Langlade, who is generally credited as the first permanent European settler in Wisconsin, settled in Green Bay in the 1760s. The Tank Cottage, built in 1776, is the oldest standing building from the state's early years and now sits at Heritage Hill State Historical Park in neighboring Allouez.

That long history shows up in the housing stock. Winters are the main wear on a house: the January mean temperature is 16.6 degrees, and 68 days a year stay at or below freezing. Roofs, furnaces and basements take the brunt of that cold, so keep receipts for any recent work on them to show a buyer.

What do the Green Bay housing numbers show?

Green Bay is the largest of the four Wisconsin cities in this group, and it has a lower median home value than Fitchburg or Franklin. The table uses the Census Bureau's QuickFacts figures.

Estimated population, July 1, 2025106,675
Change from April 2020 estimates base-0.6%

Median value of owner-occupied homes, 2020-2024$207,200
Median gross rent, 2020-2024$932

Households, 2020-202443,790

Source: U.S. Census Bureau QuickFacts. About 85.1 percent of residents lived in the same house a year earlier, which points to a stable base of local buyers and renters.

Which Green Bay projects need a permit, and what if I skipped one?

Green Bay requires a building permit for most projects other than cosmetic ones, and the city's permit guide lists what counts. Work done without a permit can come up when a buyer or lender reviews the house, so check your own records first.

  • Permit needed: basement and bathroom alterations, decks, new window or door openings, furnace installs, plumbing and electrical work, structural roofing changes, and a water heater that changes between gas and electric.
  • No permit needed: new flooring, kitchen cabinet replacement, residential siding, exact window replacement, and a same-type water heater swap.
  • Rental houses: a licensed contractor must pull the permit and do the work.

An owner who lives in the house may pull permits and do the work. Fences over 50 feet and sheds over 50 square feet need permits, while smaller ones do not, although zoning setbacks still apply. A house in a regulated floodplain may also require an itemized list of improvements. If your property is in a historic district, you also need a certificate of appropriateness, so call Inspections and Enforcement at 920-448-3300 to find out. On one- and two-family jobs, the city's residential permit page says it verifies that the contracting business holds the state Dwelling Contractor Certification and Qualifier Certification before it issues a permit.

What happens to a Green Bay short-term rental permit when I sell?

The permit does not transfer. Green Bay's short-term rental rules cover any stay under 28 consecutive days, and the city's application page states that the permit is non-transferable if the property is sold. A new owner has to apply on their own.

The initial application costs $500 and a renewal costs $250. A permit runs from July 1 through June 30, and renewals open on April 1. Missing the June 30 deadline voids the permit. Applicants submit proof of registration for Brown County room tax, a Brown County Health Department inspection report, proof of insurance and a local representative who is within 30 minutes of the property. The city says review can take up to 14 business days.

If you are selling a house that has run as a rental, tell your buyer which of those steps are current. A buyer who plans to continue the rental should budget the fee and the timeline.

What must a Green Bay seller disclose to the buyer?

An owner of a one- to four-unit property must deliver a completed condition report to the buyer within 10 days after the contract is accepted, as Wisconsin Statutes chapter 709 requires. A buyer who gets it late can rescind within two business days after the 10 days run out.

The report is a disclosure and not a warranty. It defines a defect as a condition that has a significant adverse effect on value, significantly impairs health or safety, or would shorten the expected life of the premises if left unrepaired. If you are a court-appointed fiduciary who never lived in the house, you are excused. Sellers answering for a long-owned or inherited house should still read each question and answer from what they know.

How do I record the sale in Brown County and what is the transfer fee?

The seller owes a transfer fee of 30 cents per $100 of value, set by Wisconsin Statutes 77.22. A $200,000 sale carries a $600 fee. The register collects it when the deed is submitted for recording, along with an electronic transfer return signed by both sides.

Green Bay deeds go to the Brown County Register of Deeds in the Northern Building, Room 260, at 305 E. Walnut Street, phone 920-448-4470. Its posted hours for walk-in recordings are 7:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Monday through Thursday and 7:30 to 10:30 a.m. on Friday. The mailing address is P.O. Box 23600, Green Bay, WI 54305-3600. Ask the Brown County treasurer for the tax figures your closing agent needs to prorate the bill.

More questions about Green Bay, WI

Do I have to make repairs before selling a house in Green Bay?

No. A seller can sell as is, and a cash buyer accepts the house in its present condition. You still must fill out the state condition report truthfully, and open permits or code orders should be cleared up or disclosed.

Does Green Bay require a permit to replace siding?

Residential siding does not need a permit according to the city's permit guide, but roofing with structural changes, decks and furnace installs do. Call 920-448-3300 to confirm for your project.

Can a buyer keep my Green Bay short-term rental permit?

No. The permit is non-transferable when the property is sold, so the buyer has to apply for a new one and pay the $500 initial fee.

Who pays the Wisconsin transfer fee?

The seller pays it at 30 cents per $100 of value, and the Brown County Register of Deeds collects it at recording. Some transfers, such as those by will or descent, are exempt.

How long do I have to give the buyer the condition report?

Within 10 days after the contract is accepted. If the buyer gets it late, the buyer has two business days after that period to rescind and recover deposits.

What should you know before selling a house in Eau Claire, WI?

Eau Claire is the seat of Eau Claire County, with a Census Bureau estimate of 72,465 residents on July 1, 2025, up 4.4% from the 2020 base. It is a renter-heavy city, so many sales involve tenants, small multifamily buildings or houses near the university.

You can sell by listing, by owner, or to a cash buyer. The steps that decide how smoothly it goes are the same in each case: city permit records, the assessment and tax calendar, the seller disclosure report, and recording the deed with the county.

How did Eau Claire's history shape its housing?

The city sits where the Eau Claire and Chippewa rivers meet. The first permanent settlers arrived in 1845, the city was incorporated in 1872, and it began as three separate settlements: the downtown village, West Eau Claire and Shawtown. Lumber mills built the early economy, and by the 1950s the built-up area had spread east to meet Altoona, according to the city's Wikipedia entry.

Two later events changed the housing picture. The University of Wisconsin-Eau Claire opened in 1916 and moved the economy toward education, health care and manufacturing. In 1991 the Uniroyal tire plant announced its closure, which cost 1,358 jobs, and the complex is now Banbury Place, a small business incubator. A 1982 survey identified the Randall Park, Third Ward and Emery Street Bungalow historic districts, most of which reached the National Register in 1983, so older bungalows and large lumber-era houses are part of the resale market.

Part of the city lies in Chippewa County, not only Eau Claire County. If your parcel is on that side of the line, ask which county's Register of Deeds and treasurer handle your recording and tax bill.

What do Census numbers show about Eau Claire homes?

The figures below come from the Census Bureau's QuickFacts page for Eau Claire and use 2020 to 2024 estimates unless noted.

Population estimate, July 1, 202572,465
Households30,492
Owner-occupied housing rate54.4%
Median value of owner-occupied homes$247,600
Median gross rent$1,045

Persons per household2.18

Source: U.S. Census Bureau QuickFacts, Eau Claire city, Wisconsin. With barely more than half of homes owner-occupied, rental properties are a large part of what changes hands. About 78% of residents lived in the same house a year earlier, so tenants and short-stay residents make up a meaningful share of the market.

Which schools serve Eau Claire neighborhoods?

The Eau Claire Area School District lists Memorial High School, North High School and McKinley Secondary School, three middle schools (DeLong, Northstar and South) and a long list of elementary schools that includes Flynn, Lakeshore, Locust Lane, Longfellow, Manz, Meadowview, Northwoods, Putnam Heights, Robbins, Roosevelt, Sam Davey and Sherman.

Ask the district office which school a given address feeds before you advertise the house, and do the same for parcels near the edge of the city, which may sit in a different district.

How does Eau Claire assess property and collect tax?

The City of Eau Claire sets a January 1 assessment date, and the tax bill is due in full January 31 or in two installments on January 31 and July 31. Assessment change notices usually go out between the end of April and the end of May, and the Board of Review meets during a 45-day window that opens on the fourth Monday in April.

  • Talk to an assessor first. The city says that informal meeting shows how your value was set.
  • If you still disagree, you can appeal the Board's decision to the Department of Revenue within 20 days of receiving it, with a $100 filing fee, when the value in dispute is $1 million or less.
  • A court appeal must be made within 90 days after the Board of Review adjourns, and it is decided on the record from your hearing.

The assessor's office is at 715-839-4926, and property records are searchable through the city's Beacon tool. Because tax is billed for the whole year, your closing will prorate it between you and the buyer, and the title company can show the split. Ask the Eau Claire County treasurer for the status of any unpaid bill on the parcel.

What permit and rental rules apply to Eau Claire houses?

The city's Inspection Services Division reviews plans, issues permits and inspects construction and remodeling work covering building, heating, air conditioning, electrical and plumbing. It also enforces ordinances on floodplain, zoning, property upkeep and land use. Inspection requests run through the Evolve portal or by phone, not by email to individual inspectors.

Short-term rentals have a separate set of rules that affect how a buyer can use the house. On December 10, 2024 the City Council created Chapter 5.66 and a Short-Term Rental License.

  • An owner applies first for a Tourist Rooming House license through the city-county Health Department (715-839-4718).
  • The city license is reviewed by Planning and Zoning (715-839-4914), with a parking count, a building plan and a trash container sketch.
  • The initial review fee is $700 and the annual renewal is $300, and licenses run from June 30 to June 30.
  • The council removed the proposed seven-night minimum and 180-day annual cap.

If your house has operated as a short-term rental, confirm the license status with Planning before you list, since buyers who want to continue the use will ask.

How do you transfer a deed in Eau Claire County?

Deeds are recorded with the Eau Claire County Register of Deeds, which files deeds, mortgages, satisfactions, plats and certified survey maps. Since January 1, 2025 a postage-paid envelope has to be supplied for the return of paper documents. The county's land records page lists forms, the electronic transfer return, a checklist for recording and a filing fee schedule, so check the current fee there or at rod@eauclairecounty.gov.

Wis. Stat. 77.22 charges the grantor 30 cents for each $100 of value, and the register collects it when the deed is submitted. The register has no duty to check the value you report. For a gift or a deed with nominal consideration, Wis. Stat. 77.21 uses the estimated open-market price, which matters when a family member buys at a discount.

What does the Wisconsin seller disclosure require in Eau Claire?

Chapter 709 requires owners of one-to-four-unit property to give the buyer a completed condition report within 10 days after the contract is accepted. In a condominium sale the owner also supplies an addendum with condominium information at the same time. A buyer who does not receive the report can rescind within two business days after the 10 days run out and recover deposits.

Personal representatives, trustees, conservators and court-supervised fiduciaries who never lived in the house are excused. The excusal is limited to those fiduciaries, so an ordinary owner, including a landlord, completes the report.

Is a cash sale or a listing better in Eau Claire?

A listing works when the house shows well and you can handle showings and a lender's timeline. A cash sale fits a house with deferred repairs, a tenant in place, a probate timeline or a payoff date.

Ask for a net sheet with any offer. It should list the loan payoff, the $3 per $1,000 transfer fee, recording, prorated tax and repair credits, so the offers compare on proceeds.

More questions about Eau Claire, WI

Who records deeds for Eau Claire properties?

The Eau Claire County Register of Deeds records them. Provide a postage-paid return envelope for paper documents, and check the county's filing fee schedule before you submit.

When are Eau Claire property taxes due?

January 31 in full, or in two installments on January 31 and July 31. The assessment date is January 1.

How much is the transfer fee on an Eau Claire sale?

It is 30 cents per $100 of value, paid by the seller under Wis. Stat. 77.22. A $250,000 sale carries a $750 fee.

Do I need a license to run a short-term rental in Eau Claire?

Yes. Eau Claire requires a Tourist Rooming House license from the Health Department and a city Short-Term Rental License, with a $700 initial review fee and a $300 annual renewal.

Can I appeal my Eau Claire assessment after the Board of Review?

Yes. You can appeal to the Wisconsin Department of Revenue within 20 days of the decision, with a $100 filing fee, or to circuit court within 90 days after the Board adjourns.

What are my options for selling a house fast in Fond du Lac?

A Fond du Lac owner can list the house with an agent, sell it directly to a buyer, or take a cash offer, and a cash sale gives you the most control over the closing date. The right choice turns on the house's condition and the reason you are selling.

  • List it: a fit for a house in good order and a seller who can host showings through a typical marketing period.
  • Sell it yourself: you set the price and write up the terms, and you take on the paperwork the state requires.
  • Cash offer: a fit for houses with deferred repairs, inherited homes, rentals and sellers who need a firm date.

Fond du Lac's housing costs are modest. The Census Bureau reports a median owner-occupied home value of $173,700 for 2020-2024, so repair costs weigh more heavily against the price than they do in higher-priced Wisconsin suburbs. Get a written quote before you decide whether to fix the house or sell it as is, and compare that cost with what the repair would add to your sale price.

What should a seller know about Fond du Lac?

Fond du Lac is the seat of Fond du Lac County and sits at the southern end of Lake Winnebago, which is how it got its French name meaning the bottom of the lake. Wikipedia lists the city's area as 20.54 square miles, of which 19.23 are land. The east and west branches of the Fond du Lac River join inside the city and flow into the lake near Lakeside Park, a recreation area of more than 400 acres.

The first railroad reached the community in 1852, and logging and milling drove its growth in the late 1800s. The city has four historic districts: South Main Street, North Main Street, Linden Street, and East Division and Sheboygan Streets, plus about 20 listings on the National Register of Historic Places. If your house is older, ask the city's Inspection Services office whether any special review applies before you plan exterior work.

Because the city sits on a lake and two river branches, floodplain rules are part of what the Inspection Division enforces, along with zoning and property maintenance. Confirm the flood status of your parcel before you quote a closing date.

How does the Fond du Lac housing market compare on paper?

Fond du Lac has the lowest median home value of the four cities in this group and a stable population. The table draws on the Census Bureau's QuickFacts page.

Source: U.S. Census Bureau QuickFacts. About 86.4 percent of residents lived in the same house one year earlier, so most buyers and renters here are already local. Owners with a mortgage report median monthly costs of $1,351, compared with median gross rent of $913, and the mean commute to work is 19.3 minutes.

Which repairs need a permit in Fond du Lac?

Fond du Lac requires a permit for most work on a house, and the city has adopted the state's building, mechanical, electrical and plumbing codes. According to the Building Inspections page, permits cover new buildings, additions, interior and exterior alterations, siding, roofing, garages, decks, windows, pools, sheds, patios, fences, electrical work, water heater and furnace replacements, and plumbing.

The city building inspector may waive a permit for minor alterations or maintenance repairs. To find out whether yours qualifies, call the Building Inspection office at 920-322-3570. The city also takes code violation reports through a reporting form. It publishes separate packets for fences, decks, sheds, pools, ramps and garages, which show what a finished project should include.

  • List each project you completed in the last several years and mark which ones had permits.
  • Ask Inspection Services about any open permit that still needs a final inspection.
  • Gather receipts and contractor names for roofing, windows, siding and the furnace.

The city's Housing and Code Enforcement page says municipal code covers property maintenance and public nuisance issues. If you have received a notice about the house, resolve it or disclose it before you sign a contract.

What disclosure form does a Fond du Lac seller fill out?

You complete the real estate condition report if you are transferring one to four dwelling units, and you must hand it to the buyer within 10 days of an accepted offer. Chapter 709 of the Wisconsin Statutes makes this a rule for sales, exchanges and land contracts, unless the transfer is exempt from the state transfer fee.

The form uses the word aware to mean that you have notice or knowledge of a condition. If you give written information from an engineer, surveyor, pest control operator or contractor, you can use it in place of your own answer for the matching entry, as long as it arrives on time and is clearly tied to that entry. A late report lets the buyer rescind in writing within two business days of the end of the 10-day window.

The statute's own wording says the report is not a warranty by the owner and not a substitute for inspections the parties may want. Expect a buyer to order an inspection anyway, and keep your answers consistent with anything you have already told the city or your insurer.

Where is a Fond du Lac deed recorded and what does it cost?

You record the deed at the Fond du Lac County Register of Deeds, 160 S. Macy Street, first floor, and the standard recording fee is $30. The office is open 7:45 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. on weekdays except holidays, and it records real estate documents between 7:45 a.m. and 3:30 p.m. Documents that arrive later are recorded the next business day. The phone number is 920-929-3018.

The office accepts documents by e-recording, mail or in person, and its LandShark system lets you search and buy recorded documents going back to 1839. Owners can also sign up for Land Notification alerts that warn them when a document is recorded against their name or parcel number.

The state transfer fee is 30 cents per $100 of value, and it is owed by the seller under section 77.22. On a $175,000 sale, the fee is $525. A transfer return must be filed electronically and signed by both sides. Ask the county treasurer what is owed on the property tax bill so the closing agent can split it between you and the buyer.

More questions about Fond du Lac, WI

Can I sell my Fond du Lac house as is?

Yes. You can offer the house in its present condition, and a cash buyer will price it based on what it needs. You still owe the buyer the condition report on any one- to four-unit property.

How much does it cost to record a deed in Fond du Lac County?

The standard real estate recording fee is $30 per document. The state transfer fee of 30 cents per $100 of value is separate and is paid by the seller.

What hours does the Fond du Lac County Register of Deeds keep?

The office is open 7:45 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Monday through Friday except holidays. Real estate documents are recorded between 7:45 a.m. and 3:30 p.m., and later submissions are recorded the next business day.

Do I need a permit to replace my roof or windows in Fond du Lac?

Roofing and windows are on the city's list of work that needs a permit. The building inspector can waive a permit for minor maintenance, so call 920-322-3570 to ask before you start.

What if I inherited a house in Fond du Lac and never lived there?

A court-appointed personal representative or trustee who never occupied the house is excused from the condition report, and transfers by will or descent are exempt from the transfer fee. Ask the register of deeds how to record the paperwork.

What should you know before selling a house in Brookfield, WI?

Brookfield is a city in eastern Waukesha County with an estimated 41,448 residents as of July 1, 2025, so a sale here is shaped by suburban Milwaukee-area rules and a housing stock that is mostly owner-occupied. You can list with an agent, sell on your own, or sell to a cash buyer, and the steps below apply to all three.

The items that move a Brookfield closing most are the permit history of the house, the property tax calendar, the seller's disclosure report, and the recording of the deed at the Waukesha County Register of Deeds. Each is covered below with the office to call.

What is Brookfield like for a home seller?

Brookfield was cut out of the old Town of Brookfield and incorporated as a city on August 14, 1954. At that point it had about 7,900 residents and 17.5 square miles. It now covers roughly 27.7 square miles, and the remaining piece of the town still sits along the city's western edge, according to the city's Wikipedia entry.

Postwar subdivisions drove most of that growth. The first suburban plat, Kinsey's Garvendale, dates to 1928, and building picked up after the Second World War. For a seller that history matters in a practical way: much of the housing stock dates from the postwar growth, so aging furnaces, roofs, windows and electrical panels are common repair questions from buyers.

The city has four ZIP codes (53005, 53008, 53045 and 53072) and a subcontinental divide that runs near Calhoun Road and Capitol Drive. Water east of the divide drains toward Lake Michigan, and water west of it drains toward the Fox River of Illinois and Wisconsin. If a buyer's inspector raises a drainage or basement-moisture point, the neighborhood's position relative to that divide is one fact worth knowing.

What do the Census numbers say about Brookfield housing?

The Census Bureau's QuickFacts page for Brookfield shows an owner-heavy market with high values and a small rental share. The figures below are the 2020 to 2024 estimates unless noted.

Source: U.S. Census Bureau QuickFacts, Brookfield city, Wisconsin. A median value of $443,900 means a typical Brookfield house carries a real equity position, so sellers with a mortgage payoff well below value have more room to choose between a market listing and a fast private sale.

Which school district serves a house in Brookfield?

Most Brookfield addresses are in the School District of Elmbrook, which the district describes as serving the cities of Brookfield and New Berlin and the village of Elm Grove, with more than 7,800 students. Its two main high schools are Brookfield Central and Brookfield East.

Not every parcel is in Elmbrook. The city's tax billing page lists Elmbrook Schools, the School District of Waukesha or the Hamilton School District, depending on where the property sits. Before you tell a buyer which schools apply, check the school line on the tax bill or ask the city assessor's office, since the school district is one of the first questions buyers ask.

Which permits and repairs can hold up a Brookfield sale?

Open or missing permits are the most common local snag. The city's Building Inspection office lists the work that typically needs a permit, and buyers' inspectors often ask for permit records on projects like these:

  • Additions, interior or exterior alterations, and recreation rooms
  • Decks, garages, gazebos and accessory buildings
  • Kitchen remodels and cabinet replacement, which can require building, electrical and plumbing permits
  • Furnaces, air conditioners, water heaters, dishwashers and garbage disposals (electrical or plumbing permits, depending on the item)
  • Re-roofing, re-siding and foundation repairs
  • Swimming pools and hot tubs

The city's permit page lists an online residential building permit, effective January 2, 2026, that covers one- and two-dwelling structures. The city also states that contractors must show the right State of Wisconsin credentials before they can pull a permit. If you finished a basement or replaced a water heater without paperwork, call Building Inspections at 262-796-6646 before you list. Sorting it out before a buyer's inspection avoids a surprise during negotiation.

How do property taxes work when you sell in Brookfield?

The City of Brookfield mails real estate tax bills around December 15 each year. A bill can be paid in full by January 31, or in two installments: the first to the city by January 31 and the second to the Waukesha County Treasurer by July 31. After January 31 the city treasurer stops accepting real estate payments, and checks go to the county treasurer instead.

The city collects for itself, the school district, Waukesha County and Waukesha County Technical College on one combined bill. Wisconsin's lottery and gaming credit and the first dollar credit appear on that bill. For 2025 the city reported a lottery credit of $169.02 for most taxpayers and a first dollar credit of $56.34 for most improved parcels.

  • The assessor's office values real property under Chapter 70 of the Wisconsin Statutes and the Wisconsin Property Assessment Manual.
  • The city has posted a 2026 preliminary assessment roll and an interactive web map with assessment data.
  • The tax key number on a Brookfield bill starts with the letters BRC.

How the current year's tax is split between you and the buyer is set in the purchase contract and worked out by the title company. Ask the title company for the proration figure before closing, and ask the Brookfield Treasurer at 262-787-3513 about the status of any open bill.

What does it take to transfer title in Waukesha County?

A deed has to be recorded with the Waukesha County Register of Deeds, and Wisconsin attaches a transfer fee to most sales. Under Wis. Stat. 77.22 the grantor pays 30 cents for each $100 of value, which works out to $900 on a $300,000 sale. A Real Estate Transfer Return signed by both sides has to be filed electronically with the Department of Revenue before the register will accept the deed.

The county's recording fee for a standard deed is $30, and the county accepts payment by check or money order only. A document that is eRecorded comes back right away. A paper document returns the same day if you supply an email address, or in two to three weeks if you provide a stamped envelope. The Register of Deeds does not prepare deeds or give legal advice, so the deed itself usually comes from a title company or an attorney.

Separately, Chapter 709 requires most sellers to give the buyer a completed real estate condition report within 10 days after the contract is accepted. If it is late, the buyer has two business days after that 10-day window to rescind. Personal representatives and trustees who never lived in the house are excused from the report, which matters for inherited Brookfield homes.

Should you sell to a cash buyer or list in Brookfield?

It depends on how much time and repair money you have. A listing in a market with a median value near $444,000 can reach more buyers, but it brings showings, inspection requests and a closing date that depends on the buyer's lender.

  • List with an agent when the house is in good condition, you have time, and you can cover pre-sale repairs and the commission.
  • Sell to a cash buyer when the house needs work, is occupied by tenants, has unpaid taxes or a payoff deadline, or you inherited it and want to close without staging.
  • Sell on your own if you are comfortable with the disclosure report, contract and title steps above.

Whichever route you take, compare the net figure after payoff, transfer fee, recording fee, prorated taxes and any repair credits rather than the headline price. Ask for the offer in writing and have the title company confirm the payoff and closing costs.

More questions about Brookfield, WI

How much is the transfer fee when I sell a house in Brookfield?

It is 30 cents per $100 of value, charged to the seller, so a $400,000 sale carries a $1,200 fee. The rate comes from Wis. Stat. 77.22 and applies in every Wisconsin county, and it is collected by the Waukesha County Register of Deeds when the deed is recorded.

Who records the deed for a Brookfield home?

The Waukesha County Register of Deeds records it. The standard recording fee is $30, paid by check or money order, and the electronic transfer return must be completed on the Department of Revenue site first.

When are Brookfield property taxes due?

Taxes are due in full by January 31, or in two installments on January 31 and July 31. Bills go out around December 15. After January 31 payments go to the Waukesha County Treasurer.

Do I need to give the buyer a disclosure report in Brookfield?

Yes, in most cases. Chapter 709 requires a completed real estate condition report within 10 days after the contract is accepted. Fiduciaries such as personal representatives who never occupied the home are excused.

Which Brookfield office handles building permit questions before a sale?

Building Inspections handles them at 262-796-6646. Ask whether permits were closed out for any addition, deck, furnace, water heater or remodel, since buyers' inspectors often look for that paperwork.

How do I sell a house fast in Franklin, WI?

The fastest route is a cash sale, which skips the buyer's mortgage approval, and the slowest is a listing that waits on showings and a lender. Franklin sellers can also sell on their own, so the real question is how much time and repair work you can absorb.

  • Agent listing: a good fit for a well-kept house when you can wait for the best financed offer.
  • Owner sale: you handle the pricing, showings, contract and state disclosure form.
  • Cash buyer: a fit for a house with deferred maintenance, a divorce or estate sale, a move on a deadline, or a rental you no longer want to manage.

Franklin is a city where most homes are owner-occupied. The Census Bureau puts the rate at 77.3 percent for 2020-2024, so a typical seller here owns a house they have lived in. Nearly one resident in five, 19.6 percent, is 65 or older, so estate and downsizing sales are a regular part of the local picture.

What should a seller know about Franklin's layout and history?

Franklin is a city in southern Milwaukee County that borders Oak Creek to the east, Greendale, Hales Corners and Greenfield to the north, Racine County to the south and Waukesha County to the west. Wikipedia gives its land area as 34.58 square miles, and the Root River runs south through the city and divides it.

The Town of Franklin was split off from the Town of Kinnikinick on December 20, 1839, and was named for Benjamin Franklin. By the 1950s it was known as a City of Homes because of its growing residential neighborhoods. Town officials feared Milwaukee might annex part of their land, so they incorporated Franklin as a fourth-class city on August 15, 1956.

The city sits about four miles from Milwaukee Mitchell International Airport and close to Interstate 94. U.S. Highway 45 and Wisconsin highways 36, 100 and 241 pass through it. When you describe your house to a buyer, say where it sits relative to those roads, the Root River and the airport, since location is part of what any buyer will weigh.

What do the Franklin housing numbers show?

Franklin has the highest household income of the four cities in this group, and its median home value is $364,200. The Census Bureau's QuickFacts page is the source for the table below.

Source: U.S. Census Bureau QuickFacts. Some 92.5 percent of residents lived in the same house a year earlier, which points to low turnover. Owners with a mortgage report median monthly costs of $2,218, owners without one report $895, and the mean commute is 23.3 minutes.

What work on a Franklin house needs a permit?

Franklin requires a permit to build a new structure, add to a house, make structural changes, and for a long list of other jobs. The city's Inspection Services FAQ names accessory buildings, residing, reroofing, fences, decks, swimming pools and HVAC. Permits must be in hand before work starts.

  • Electrical and plumbing work must be done by licensed contractors who pull their own permits.
  • A homeowner can do other work, but the owner is responsible for the permit even if a contractor was supposed to get it.
  • Residential permits are processed in the order received, and the city asks you to allow at least 10 business days. Contractors applying for one- and two-family work must hold valid state certifications.

If a past contractor never pulled a permit, call Inspection Services at 414-425-0084. The office is at 9229 W. Loomis Road and is open weekdays from 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Staff will help you obtain the required permits and inspections, though the city cannot settle a dispute between you and the contractor.

If you plan fixes before listing, remember the noise rule in the city code: operating tools or equipment between 9 p.m. and 7 a.m. is a violation when it creates a noise disturbance. A cash buyer may take the house without those fixes, which can save you the time of managing contractors.

What disclosures must a Franklin seller provide?

A Franklin seller must give the buyer a real estate condition report within 10 days after an offer is accepted, and a buyer who does not receive it can rescind. This comes from Wisconsin Statutes chapter 709, which applies to property with one to four dwelling units.

The buyer may rescind within two business days after the 10-day period ends and is entitled to a refund of deposits. If the property is a condominium unit, you must also attach an addendum that names the condominium and its association, lists current assessments and special charges, and says whether they have been paid. A personal representative, trustee or conservator who never occupied the house is not required to complete the report.

Sellers often ask whether a cash sale changes any of this. The statute applies to any sale, exchange or land contract of that kind of property, and it does not turn on how the buyer pays. If the transfer is exempt from the state transfer fee, such as an inheritance by will, the report is excused as well.

How is a Franklin sale recorded and what is the transfer fee?

The deed is recorded with the Milwaukee County Register of Deeds, 901 N. 9th Street, Room 103, Milwaukee, and the seller pays a state transfer fee of 30 cents for each $100 of value. On a $350,000 sale the fee is $1,050. The statute behind it is section 77.22.

The county's recording page says each document costs $30 to record, and every conveyance needs an electronic transfer return receipt. The office accepts cash, checks or money orders, but not credit or debit cards. Documents are recorded in order of receipt within three to five business days, and the original is mailed back in one to two weeks. For recording questions, call 414-278-4005. For help with the transfer return, call the Department of Revenue at 608-266-1594.

If you inherited a Franklin house, a transfer by will or descent is exempt from the fee under section 77.25. The register's office does not supply deed forms and cannot give legal advice, so use an attorney or title company to prepare the paperwork. When a spouse has died and both names are on the deed, the county describes a Termination of Decedent's Interest form, recorded with a $30 fee and a transfer return that claims the 77.25 (11) exemption. Ask the Milwaukee County treasurer for the tax balance so your closing agent can prorate it.

What is the fastest way to sell a house in Franklin?

A cash sale is usually the fastest, because the buyer does not need a lender's approval. A listing takes longer since it depends on showings, offers, inspections and financing.

Do I need a permit to replace a roof in Franklin?

Yes. The city lists reroofing among the work that needs a permit, along with siding, fences, decks, pools and HVAC. Call Inspection Services at 414-425-0084 to confirm what applies.

Where do I record a deed for a Franklin property?

At the Milwaukee County Register of Deeds, 901 N. 9th Street, Room 103, Milwaukee. Bring the original deed, the electronic transfer return receipt and the $30 recording fee.

How much is the Wisconsin real estate transfer fee?

It is 30 cents for each $100 of value, paid by the seller. Some transfers are exempt, including transfers by will or descent.

Can I sell an inherited house in Franklin without living in it?

Yes. A court-appointed personal representative or trustee who never occupied the house does not have to complete the condition report. Use a deed and the electronic transfer return, and ask the register of deeds how to clear a deceased owner's name from title.

What are the ways to sell a house in Fitchburg?

A Fitchburg owner can list with an agent, sell without one, or accept a cash offer from a buyer who takes the house in its current condition. Each route moves at a different speed and puts different work on you, so the right pick depends on the shape of the house and how soon you need to close.

  • List with an agent: best for a house in good repair when you can leave it open for showings and wait for a financed buyer.
  • Sell it yourself: you price, market, negotiate and handle the paperwork, including the state condition report described below.
  • Cash offer: suited to a house that needs work, a tenant situation, an inherited property or a tight deadline. The buyer usually skips the repair negotiation and lender timeline.

Fitchburg has a lot of rental housing. The Census Bureau puts the owner-occupied rate at 47.6 percent for 2020-2024, which means many sellers here are landlords or heirs of a house that has had tenants, not only owners moving out of a home they lived in.

What should a Fitchburg seller know about the city?

Fitchburg is a Dane County city that sits directly south of Madison and belongs to the Madison metropolitan area. According to Wikipedia's city profile, it combines suburban neighborhoods near the Madison line, commercial and industrial land, and rural property in the south.

The area was farmed from 1837 and organized as the Town of Greenfield in 1847. It took the name Fitchburg in 1853 to avoid confusion with Greenfield in Milwaukee County. When Madison began annexing town land, Fitchburg pursued incorporation to stop it. The dispute went to the Wisconsin Supreme Court, which ruled for Fitchburg, and the city incorporated on April 26, 1983.

That history explains the variety of homes. A buyer or cash purchaser looking at a house near the Madison border sees a very different lot, age and street pattern than one looking at a property near Fitchburg Center or the southern edge. Areas named in the city's bus routes and station plans include Southdale, High Ridge Trail, Greenway Crossing, Terravessa and Fitchburg Center. The Badger State Trail and the Ice Age Trail pass through the city, and Metro Transit runs routes connecting parts of Fitchburg to downtown Madison.

How do Fitchburg housing numbers look right now?

Fitchburg is growing quickly, and its median home value sits above $400,000. The figures below come from the Census Bureau's QuickFacts page for Fitchburg.

Two more figures help frame a sale. Owners with a mortgage report median monthly costs of $2,384, and workers spend a mean of 18.9 minutes getting to work. Both numbers come from the same QuickFacts table, and both point to a commuter city with a short drive into Madison.

Which Fitchburg permits and inspections matter before a sale?

Fitchburg's Building Inspection Department handles permits for work on a house, and a buyer or lender can ask about any permit that should exist for past repairs. The department enforces the 2021 International Building Code, the 2017 National Electrical Code and the 2016 Uniform Dwelling Code for one- and two-family homes, and permit applications go through the city's online OpenGov portal.

If you finished a basement, replaced a furnace or added a deck without a permit, tell the inspectors before you list. You can call the general line at 608-270-4240 or visit 5520 Lacy Road. Closing a permit gap before you list keeps it from surfacing during the buyer's review. A cash buyer will often take the house as it stands, but you still owe truthful answers on the state disclosure form.

Ask the Building Inspection Department what inspections an open permit still needs, and keep the final sign-off with your sale file.

What if the Fitchburg house has been a short-term rental?

Fitchburg requires short-term rental properties to be licensed, and the license year runs from July 1 to June 30. The city's application page lists a $150 fee, proof of property and liability insurance, and a copy of the Public Health Madison and Dane County hotel, motel or tourist rooming house license.

If you operate a short-term rental and plan to sell, ask the city whether the license carries over to a new owner. Also cancel upcoming guest bookings that run past your expected closing date. Sellers who rent long term should check the lease end date and the tenant's notice rights before setting a closing date.

What disclosure paperwork does a Fitchburg seller owe the buyer?

A seller of a home with one to four dwelling units must give the buyer a completed real estate condition report within 10 days after the contract is accepted, under Wisconsin Statutes chapter 709. If the buyer does not get it in time, the buyer has two business days after the 10-day period ends to rescind in writing and recover deposits.

The form asks about defects you know of, and each item must be answered. A court-appointed personal representative, trustee or conservator who never lived in the house is excused from the form, which matters for estate sales. Transfers that are exempt from the state transfer fee are excused as well.

  • Answer every line, even if the answer is that you are not aware of a problem.
  • Attach written reports from an engineer, surveyor or pest operator if you want to rely on them for an entry.
  • Use the form the statute prescribes, and correct it if something changes before closing.

How is the deed recorded and what does the transfer fee cost?

The seller pays a real estate transfer fee of 30 cents for each $100 of value, which works out to $3 per $1,000 of price. Wisconsin Statutes section 77.22 sets the rate, and the register of deeds collects it when the deed is submitted. On a $400,000 sale, the fee comes to $1,200.

Fitchburg deeds are recorded with the Dane County Register of Deeds. A deed must identify the grantor and grantee, carry the grantor's notarized signature and a legal description, and show the parcel number from the tax bill. Only the original deed is recorded, and an electronic transfer return receipt must come with it. The recording fee is $30 per document, and the mailing address is PO Box 1438, Madison, WI 53701-1438.

Some transfers carry no fee. Section 77.25 exempts transfers by will or descent and gifts between parent and child for nominal or no consideration, among others, and the reason must be stated on the deed. Ask the county treasurer for the property tax amounts due so your closing agent can split them correctly.

More questions about Fitchburg, WI

How fast can I sell my house in Fitchburg?

It depends on the route. A cash purchase can close on the date you choose, while a listed sale usually needs time for showings, an offer, the buyer's inspection and a lender's approval. Whichever route you pick, the condition report is due within 10 days of acceptance.

Do I need a permit record to sell a Fitchburg house?

Buyers and lenders often ask about past work, although no single record is required to close. Call Fitchburg Building Inspection at 608-270-4240 to ask whether a permit exists or is still open for repairs you made.

Who pays the transfer fee on a Fitchburg sale?

The seller. Wisconsin imposes the fee on the grantor at 30 cents per $100 of value, and the Dane County Register of Deeds collects it when the deed is recorded.

Can I sell a Fitchburg house with tenants in it?

Yes. Read the lease for its end date and any notice terms, and give the buyer a copy. A buyer who wants the house empty may need to agree on a move-out date with the tenant.

Where do I record the deed for a Fitchburg property?

With the Dane County Register of Deeds, because Fitchburg is in Dane County. The office takes the original deed, the electronic transfer return receipt and a $30 recording fee.

What does selling a house in De Pere, WI involve?

De Pere is a city in Brown County, about five miles south of Green Bay on the Fox River, with a 2025 Census Bureau estimate of 25,590 residents. A sale here runs through three local offices: the City of De Pere for permits and assessment, the Brown County Register of Deeds for the deed, and the Brown County Treasurer for tax records.

You can list with an agent, sell on your own, or accept a cash offer from a buyer who takes the house as it stands. The sections below cover the De Pere details that affect price and timing under each route.

What is De Pere like, and how does the layout affect a home sale?

De Pere grew up around the first and last rapids on the lower Fox River. A French Jesuit mission was founded there in 1671, and the city traces its modern plat to 1836, when the De Pere Hydraulic Company laid out the town. The east and west banks were separate municipalities for decades. East De Pere became a city in 1883, and West De Pere (briefly named Nicolet) was folded into it in 1890, according to the city's Wikipedia entry.

That two-bank history still shapes the market. Large older homes line Broadway, Ridgeway Boulevard, Morris, Fulton, Franklin and nearby streets close to the river, and several of those blocks sit in National Register historic districts. St. Norbert College, founded in 1898, borders the river on the west side. Newer subdivisions sit away from the water, with Interstate 41 running along the west side of the city and Highways 32 and 57 entering from the south.

The city says two school districts serve De Pere, so check which one covers your address before you tell a buyer. Wikipedia also notes that the Lower Fox River below the De Pere dam went through a cleanup of PCB-contaminated sediment that was completed in 2020. If you are selling a riverfront house, buyers are likely to ask about it, so it helps to have the answer ready.

What do Census figures say about De Pere housing?

How does De Pere assess property, and what can you do about it?

Since 2018 De Pere has reassessed every property each year, so the city's values stay close to market. The city contracts the work to Accurate Appraisal, LLC of Menasha, and its assessment page explains that an assessor does not set tax rates and that a revaluation does not raise the total tax the city collects. The city's own explainer reported an overall average increase of about 8 to 10 percent in the 2024 update.

  • Open Book is a short conference, in person or by phone, with an assessor to review your value.
  • If you still disagree, you can appeal to the Board of Review, a five-member board of residents appointed by the mayor.
  • You schedule that appearance through the City Clerk at 339-4050 and file a Formal Objection Application. State law treats the assessor's value as correct until you prove otherwise with facts.

The city tells owners to call the Brown County Treasurer at (920) 448-4074 when the mailing address for a property changes, so tax bills reach the right person. After a sale, give the treasurer the buyer's mailing address so the next bill goes to the right place, and ask the title company how the current year's tax is split at closing.

Which De Pere permit rules matter before you sell?

The city's Building Inspection page tells buyers they can request city building records to see whether permits were obtained and whether work passed inspection. That makes permit history a negotiation point. Before listing, ask the Building Department (920-339-4053, dpbldg@deperewi.gov) for the record on your parcel.

  • A permit is required for new construction, repairs, additions, alterations and demolitions, including boilers, furnaces, wiring, plumbing fixtures, garages, porches, fences, decks, swimming pools and sheds.
  • Starting work without a permit doubles the permit fee, and a stop work order can follow.
  • A building permit lasts one year, or two years for a one- or two-family dwelling.
  • Replacing windows or changing exits and light openings can also need a permit.

The city warns that projects not completed to code can affect a home's insurability and potential sale. If you find open work, finishing and closing the permit before you list often settles the question for a buyer. If you cannot meet zoning or code requirements, the Zoning Board of Appeals hears variance requests for a $175 fee.

Can you rent out a De Pere house before selling it?

Long-term tenants are common in De Pere, and the city also regulates short-term rentals. Anyone who rents a house on a platform like Airbnb or VRBO needs a Tourist Rooming House license, which in De Pere is a two-step process. You first apply to the Development Services Department with a $100 fee, and after approval the Health Department's sanitarian explains how to get the license. The city says you may not rent the property until the sanitarian completes a pre-inspection.

If your house has been used as a short-term rental, ask the city's Development Services Department about its license status before you list. A buyer who plans to continue the use will ask.

How do you record the deed at the Brown County Register of Deeds?

De Pere deeds are recorded at the Brown County Register of Deeds, Northern Building Room 260, 305 E. Walnut Street, Green Bay. The office is open Monday to Thursday 7:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. and Friday 7:30 to 11:30 a.m., and walk-in real estate recordings are accepted until 4:30 p.m. Monday through Thursday and until 10:30 a.m. on Friday. The phone number is 920-448-4470.

Brown County has moved to tag-less recording. If you submit paper documents, you also submit a Swift Agreement, and you receive an email with a secure link that allows up to three printed copies for seven days.

The deed also needs the state transfer return. Wis. Stat. 77.22 sets the fee at 30 cents per $100 of value, paid by the grantor, and requires the return to be filed electronically. The register writes the fee on the face of the deed, and if a sale is exempt, the exemption reason must be stated on the deed.

What must a De Pere seller disclose to the buyer?

Chapter 709 applies to sales, exchanges and land contracts of property with one to four dwelling units, and to vacant land. The chapter's definition excludes dwellings that have never been inhabited. The owner completes the state's condition report and delivers it within 10 days after the contract is accepted.

If the report is late, the buyer has a short window to cancel. Personal representatives, trustees and conservators who never occupied the home are excused, which helps heirs selling an estate house in De Pere. Everyone else should answer every item, because a partly filled report is treated as incomplete.

Should you list, or sell your De Pere house for cash?

A listing suits a house that shows well and a seller who can wait on a buyer's financing. A cash sale suits a house with open permits, deferred maintenance, tenants, or a family estate to close.

Whatever the route, ask for a net sheet. It should show the loan payoff, the 30 cents per $100 transfer fee, recording, prorated taxes and any repair credit, so you compare actual proceeds and not asking prices.

Who assesses property in De Pere?

Accurate Appraisal, LLC of Menasha, under contract with the city. De Pere has assessed every property annually since 2018, and owners can attend an Open Book session to discuss a value.

Where is a De Pere deed recorded?

At the Brown County Register of Deeds in Green Bay. The office phone is 920-448-4470, and paper submissions need a Swift Agreement under the county's tag-less system.

What is the Wisconsin transfer fee on a De Pere sale?

It is 30 cents for each $100 of value, paid by the seller. On a $280,000 sale that is $840.

Can I rent my De Pere house on Airbnb before I sell?

Only with a Tourist Rooming House license. The city requires a $100 application to Development Services and a pre-inspection by the Health Department sanitarian before any rental.

Does unpermitted work stop a De Pere sale?

Buyers can request the city's building records, and open work can come up in negotiation. Starting work without a permit doubles the permit fee, so closing out permits before listing is usually cheaper.

What should a seller in Caledonia, WI know first?

Caledonia is a village in the northeast corner of Racine County, with 25,361 residents at the 2020 census and a Census Bureau estimate of 25,229 on July 1, 2025. Selling a house here means dealing with the village for assessment and permit history, and with Racine County for recording the deed.

Your realistic options are a listing with an agent, a sale by owner, or a direct sale to a cash buyer. Which one fits depends on the condition of the house, whether it sits in the village's older neighborhoods or on a larger rural lot, and how soon you need to close.

How is Caledonia laid out, and why does it matter for a sale?

The village covers about 45 square miles along Lake Michigan, which makes it large by Wisconsin standards. It is made up of distinct communities: Franksville (the old Skunk Grove trading area), Husher, Tabor and others that began as trading posts, railroad stops and crossroads, according to the village's own history page. A buyer looking at a Franksville lot is comparing a different setting from someone looking near Douglas Avenue, and your listing or offer conversation should reflect that.

The village describes easy access to I-94, with Milwaukee 18 miles north and Chicago 73 miles south, plus two business parks (Caledonia and DeBack Farms) that supply local jobs. It also notes the planned Microsoft development in neighboring Mount Pleasant. Commute length matters to buyers, and Census data puts the mean travel time to work for Caledonia residents at 25.8 minutes.

The land has deep roots. An Indian-French fur trader, Jacques Vieau, ran a trading post here around 1832, the Town of Caledonia was created by a territorial act on February 7, 1842, and Bohemian farmers settled in the Tabor area from 1849. The area became a village in January 2006, after a 2005 referendum. For an owner, that history shows up as older farmhouses, long narrow lots near the lakeshore and mixed rural and suburban parcels.

How does the Caledonia assessor affect your sale?

The village has contracted its assessing since 1999 through Cole-Layer-Trumble, now Tyler Technologies. The assessor's job is to place market-based values on all taxable property, and the village states that the assessor does not set tax rates or collect taxes.

The 2026 appeal window has closed. Notices went out July 1, the open-book period ran July 13 to 31, the deadline to give notice of objection was August 17, and the Board of Review met August 19. If you think an assessment is too high before you list, ask the assessor's office when next year's schedule is set. An objection must be filed on form PA-115A at least 48 hours before the first Board of Review meeting, unless the board waives it for good cause.

What permits and building records come up in Caledonia?

The village Building Department issues permits for residential and commercial work, with building, electrical and plumbing inspectors on staff. New homes go through the State of Wisconsin online building permit system, and plumbing and electrical permits are pulled separately from the main application.

For a sale, the practical point is that any work on the house since you bought it should have a closed permit. A buyer's lender or inspector may ask for it, and open work can lower an offer. Call the Building Department with the parcel address and ask for the permit history before you list.

  • A septic mound system needs a sanitary permit from Racine County Planning and Development, so ask that office for records if your lot has one.
  • Rural and lakeshore parcels can have drainage, grading and culvert certifications on file, which the village requires for new homes.
  • Keep copies of final inspection sign-offs with your sale file.

How do you record a deed at the Racine County Register of Deeds?

Caledonia deeds are recorded in Racine County. The county's flat recording fee for a standard document is $30, plus the state transfer fee on the sale. Under Wis. Stat. 77.22 the grantor owes 30 cents per $100 of value, and on a land contract the value is the total principal the buyer agrees to pay.

The Wisconsin Real Estate Transfer Return can only be filed online through the Department of Revenue. The Register of Deeds can't help complete it; the county points people to the Department of Revenue at (608) 264-6885 or (608) 266-1594. A deed must also meet the county's checklist:

  • Grantor and grantee are named
  • The grantor's signature is notarized or authenticated
  • A complete legal description is included
  • The parcel identification number is shown
  • The drafter's name and a return address appear on the document
  • The document is legible and follows the state margin rules

The Racine County Register of Deeds phone number is (262) 636-3208. If the owner has died and the deed lists the decedent, ask whether a Termination of Decedent's Property Interest (form HT-110, $30 to record) applies before you sell.

What disclosure does Wisconsin require when you sell in Caledonia?

Most sellers must give the buyer a completed real estate condition report within 10 days after the contract is accepted, under Wis. Stat. 709.02. The chapter covers property with one to four dwelling units, and it also covers land with no buildings, which uses a separate vacant land report. That second category matters in a village with rural parcels.

A buyer who does not receive the report on time can rescind within two business days after the 10-day period ends and get any deposit back. Personal representatives, trustees, conservators and court-appointed fiduciaries who never occupied the property are not required to give the report. Everyone else should answer every item, since a report counts as complete only when each item is answered or covered by a permitted substitute.

Is a cash sale or a listing better in Caledonia?

A listing makes sense when the house is current on repairs and you can wait for a buyer's financing. A cash sale makes more sense when the house needs work, has a short payoff clock, or comes with tenants or an estate to settle.

Compare offers on net proceeds rather than price alone. Ask the title company to show the payoff, the transfer fee, the $30 recording fee, prorated taxes and any repair credit. If the number you would net from a listing is not much higher than a clean cash offer, the faster route can win.

Record it with the Racine County Register of Deeds. The flat recording fee is $30, and the Wisconsin Real Estate Transfer Return must be filed online with the Department of Revenue first.

How much is the Wisconsin transfer fee on a Caledonia sale?

It is 30 cents per $100 of value, charged to the seller. A $250,000 sale carries a $750 fee under Wis. Stat. 77.22.

Can I still appeal my 2026 Caledonia assessment?

No, the 2026 deadline to give notice of objection was August 17, 2026, and the Board of Review met August 19. Ask the village assessor's office for next year's dates.

Do I need a condition report to sell a house in Caledonia?

Usually yes. Chapter 709 gives you 10 days after the contract is accepted to deliver it, and the buyer may rescind if it is late. Fiduciaries who never lived in the home are excused.
